patches_submitted.subject: [PATCH] btrfs: keep unused block groups queued when a pass fails

version_history.subject: [PATCH] btrfs: keep unused block groups queued when a pass fails

patches_submitted.patch_summary: This patch addresses a potential issue in the btrfs file system where unused block groups can be leaked and lead to spurious ENOSPC errors. The problem occurs when an error is encountered while deleting unused block groups, causing them to be skipped and not re-queued for later processing. To fix this, the patch changes the logic of the deletion loop to break out of it when an error is encountered, rather than skipping the rest of the block groups. Additionally, it links the failing block group to a retry list at the individual failure sites, ensuring that it is not leaked.

review_comments.author: Qu Wenruo
review_comments.summary:
Reviewer Qu Wenruo questioned which error caused a non-zero @ret value in the loop and suggested that the issue might be due to incorrect reserved space checking by inc_block_group_ro() checks.

Reviewer noted that the patch's approach of breaking out of the loop when ret != 0 may not be sufficient, as it delays error handling to the next iteration.
review_comments.raw_body:
Do have happen to know which error caused this non-zero @ret?

I did a quick glance into the loop, it looks like it's not that easy to 
get a non-zero @ret:

- inc_block_group_ro() failure
   @ret is reset to 0, so not this path.

- btrfs_zone_finish()
   I guess meta is not deploying zoned btrfs in production.

- btrfs_star_trans_remove_block_group()
   This can return -ENOSPC, especially considering we have just marked
   one bg read-only, thus even stealing from global rsv, we may still
   fail with ENOSPC here.

   Although I'd say, that means the inc_block_group_ro() checks are not
   doing the correct reserved space checking, and that may be the real
   problem.

- btrfs_remove_chunk()
   If it failed, the trans is already aborted.

---

Otherwise the handling looks correct to me, doing the proper handling on 
error, other than delaying it to the next iteration.

Reviewed-by: Qu Wenruo <wqu@suse.com>

Thanks,
Qu

review_comments.author: Boris Burkov (author)
review_comments.summary:
Author acknowledged that they don't have concrete evidence to support their initial claim, but still believes the issue is legitimate based on reproduction by error injection.

Author agrees that ENOSPC or ENOMEM could be the cause of leaked block groups and acknowledges the reviewer's points about other potential error sites, but does not provide a clear plan for addressing these concerns.
sentiment_signals: does not provide a clear plan
review_comments.raw_body:
I do not have a trace or any other error log in dmesg to conclude where
it came from. I just have boxes with a lot of empty bgs not linked on
the unused list and inferred this mechanism.

---

I suspect ENOSPC or ENOMEM from this one, personally. Agreed with the
rest of your points on the other possible error sites.

patches_submitted.subject: [PATCH v3 3/3] btrfs: downgrade the reflink source inode lock for tree walking

version_history.subject: [PATCH v2 3/3] btrfs: downgrade the reflink source inode lock for tree walking
[PATCH v3 3/3] btrfs: downgrade the reflink source inode lock for tree walking

patches_submitted.patch_summary: This patch improves the performance of reflink operations in Btrfs by downgrading the lock on the source inode from exclusive to shared during tree walking. This is done to avoid blocking other shared lock users, such as direct I/O writers and readers, which can cause stalls. The patch also adds a new flag to indicate when an inode is being used as a reflink source, and ensures that this flag is visible to direct I/O writers. Additionally, it remains exclusive for dio reads until the inode_dio_wait() function is finished with its work.

[PATCH v3 2/3] btrfs: skip unlocked reflink source flush if the inode has writers

patches_submitted.patch_summary: This patch modifies the Btrfs reflink code to skip optimistic unlocked flushing if there are active writers dirtying pages, reducing write amplification and user-space stalls.

review_comments.author: Filipe Manana
review_comments.summary: Suggested using inode_is_open_for_write() instead of reading a counter directly to determine if an inode has writers. This change was accepted with a Reviewed-by tag.
review_comments.raw_body:
On Tue, Sep 15, 2026 at 8:05 PM Boris Burkov <boris@bur.io> wrote:
>
> The optimistic unlocked flushing is counter-productive if there is an
> active writer dirtying pages, as it results in doubly writing back any
> pages that get dirtied again before the locked flush. Therefore,
> pessimize it slightly and don't do the unlocked flushing if we have
> outstanding writable file descriptors or memory mappings. Since the
> inode isn't locked, this is only advisory, any new mapping or fd that
> sneaks in after the check but before the locking can still cause extra
> writeback. But it trivially helps quite a bit in simple cases with a
> long open file descriptor or mapping.
>
> I tested this with two similar workloads. One was keeping and fd open
> and doing continuous writes into the src file while cloning it and doing
> lseek on it and the other was slightly meaner, constantly opening and
> closing the fd to try to race this check.
>
> Workload 1 shows a huge regression in write amplification and writers
> and readers who experience userspace wall time stalls of 100ms+ with
> just the pre-flush, but recovers to normal with this check.
>
> Workload 2 is a smaller regression which is mostly helped but not fully
> resolved with this check. So we must weigh this regression against the
> benefit of the unlocked flush in the allegedly more common simpler case.
>
> Workload 1: fd kept open, 60s of clone/write/lseek looping.
> kernel        clones  clone mean s  device MiB/clone  writer stalls  reader stalls
> for-next         564         0.095               119             10             10
> pre-flush (p1)   179         0.338               405             94             93
> skip (p1+p2)     540         0.100               116              9              9
>
> Workload 2: same writer, but closing and reopening the fd around each
> 64 MiB write with some random sleeping to encourage racing.
> kernel        clones  clone mean s  device MiB/clone  writer stalls  reader stalls
> for-next         740         0.070                83              9              9
> pre-flush (p1)   255         0.224               246             27             26
> skip (p1+p2)     518         0.107               121             11             11
>
> Signed-off-by: Boris Burkov <boris@bur.io>
> ---
>  fs/btrfs/reflink.c | 14 ++++++++++----
>  1 file changed, 10 insertions(+), 4 deletions(-)
>
> diff --git a/fs/btrfs/reflink.c b/fs/btrfs/reflink.c
> index 24c0b226bc31..fe765ab27c82 100644
> --- a/fs/btrfs/reflink.c
> +++ b/fs/btrfs/reflink.c
> @@ -950,13 +950,19 @@ loff_t btrfs_remap_file_range(struct file *src_file, loff_t off,
>         /*
>          * Optimistically write out the src inode before taking locks.
>          * Consistency is properly ensured by the btrfs_wait_ordered_range()
> -        * inside btrfs_remap_file_range_prep().
> +        * inside btrfs_remap_file_range_prep(). This optimization causes
> +        * redundant writeback if there is a concurrent writer to the src file
> +        * so try to catch anyone holding the file open for writes and skip
> +        * the optimization in that case.
>          */
>         wb_start = ALIGN_DOWN(off, src_inode->root->fs_info->sectorsize);
>         wb_len = calc_remap_wb_len(src_inode, off, len, remap_flags);

> -       if (ret < 0)

> +       if (atomic_read(&src_inode->vfs_inode.i_writecount) <= 0 &&

Instead of reading the counter directly, use inode_is_open_for_write() please.

patches_submitted.subject: [PATCH v3 1/3] btrfs: pre-flush reflink source before taking inode locks

version_history.subject: [PATCH v2 1/3] btrfs: pre-flush reflink source before taking inode locks
[PATCH v3 1/3] btrfs: pre-flush reflink source before taking inode locks

patches_submitted.patch_summary: This patch optimizes the reflink operation in Btrfs by pre-flushing the source file before taking inode locks, reducing contention between writers and readers. The current logic blocks concurrent usage of inode locks during writeback, leading to performance issues. This patch introduces an optimistic btrfs_wait_ordered_range() call outside the locked region, ensuring correctness while minimizing the risk of double-writeback in case of concurrent writes. The change improves the performance of reflink operations by allowing direct reads and seeks to proceed concurrently with writeback.

patches_submitted.patch_summary: This patch reduces contention on the src inode lock during reflink operations by attempting to write back the source file outside of the lock and downgrading the lock to shared when safe. The approach involves pre-flushing the source file, skipping flush if there are writers, and then downgrading the lock for tree walking. This should improve performance in scenarios with high contention on these locks.
